chunks: Al-Shaykh informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Sindī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿĪsā ibn Abī Manṣūr, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A woman’s garment was stained with menstrual blood, and she washed it, but the trace of the blood remained on her garment. He said: “Tell her to dye it with mishq so that it blends in.”
Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: And when najasah affects something from the vessels, they are purified by washing. Its explanation has already preceded in what came before.
Al-Shaykh said, may Allah the Exalted support him: If urine falls upon the ground and then the sun shines upon it and dries it, it becomes pure by that; likewise reed mats and floor mats.
That is indicated by the following.

key_terms.أَثَرُ الدَّمِ: the remaining visible trace or mark of blood after washing
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose drying has a purifying effect in this context
key_terms.الْأَوَانِي: vessels or containers subject to purification rulings
key_terms.الْبَوَارِي وَالْحُصُرُ: reed mats and floor mats included in the ruling of purification
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine as a source of najasah
key_terms.دَمِ الْحَيْضِ: menstrual blood causing ritual impurity on clothing
key_terms.طُهِّرَتْ: was rendered pure according to legal purification rules

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the trace of menstrual blood remains on a garment after washing?
ai.summary: This passage discusses rulings of taharah concerning menstrual blood on clothing, najasah affecting vessels, and the purification of ground and mats by the sun after drying. It reflects practical fiqh guidance in Shia hadith literature regarding removal of impurity and the legal effect of washing and sun-drying.
